RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the October 20, 2008/Asvina 28, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Law
and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable Energy; Power;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and Child
Development)
Total number of questions — 20
8
Development of Chiria Mines
*21. SHRI JAI PRAKASH
NARAYAN SINGH:
SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that M/s. Arcelor
Mittal has shown interest in joining hands
with Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL),
and is open for a Joint Venture (JV)
agreement for developing the Chiria Mines;
(b) if so, the complete details in this
regard; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
resolve the ongoing dispute between SAIL
and the Jharkhand Government over Chiria
Mines?
Beggars selling children in Kolkata
†*22. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that beggars are
selling children in Kolkata;
(b) whether it is also a fact that this
practice is not being controlled due to
corruption; and
(c) if so, the details in this regard?
Judges (Inquiry) Bill
*23. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Bill, empowering the
people to complain against corrupt Judges,
would remain a pipe-dream as Government
is reportedly succumbing to pressure from
some of its allies, keen to avoid a
confrontation with the judiciary;
(b) whether this move is bound to raise
eye-brows because the Supreme Court is at
present struggling to constitute a probe panel
into the multicrore Ghaziabad Provident
Funds Scam, in which 36 Judges of the Apex
Court are allegedly involved; and
(c) if so, whether Government proposes
to shelve the Judges (Inquiry) Bill from
becoming a law and if so, the reasons
therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
Collaboration with foreign
technological universities
*24. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR:
SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to allow
foreign technological universities to
collaborate with Indian universities and
institutes, to conduct joint programmes;
(b) whether suitable regulations in this
regard have been brought out by
Government; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Overdrawal of electricity from the grid
*25. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Central Electricity
Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued
directions to State Governments to curb
overdrawal of power/electricity from the
Grid;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether inspite of directions by the
CERC, the States are violating the Indian
Electricity Grid Code and are ignoring the
instructions of the Regional Load Despatch
Centres (RLDC); and
(d) if so, the concrete steps Government
proposes to take in this regard?
Chinese power plants in India
*26. SHRI HARISH RAWA T:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Central Electricity
Authority has set up a Committee to probe
the technical quality of the Chinese plants
installed in India;
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c) whether permission to the Chinese
firms to set up power plants in the country
is posing threat to the security of the
country; and
(d) if so, the facts thereof and the steps
taken by Government to ensure that such
permission to the Chinese firms does not
pose any threat to the country?
Infrastructural facilities and human
resources in higher education
†*27. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the amount required for establishing
infrastructural facilities and human
resources for teaching to achieve the higher
education,  target of 15 per cent separately,
and in which manner and from which
sources the same would be raised;
(b) the projection as to the number of
students likely to opt for technical
education in the field of higher education
and the number of industrial establishments
which have agreed to co-opt in this field;
and
(c) whether it is a fact that the policy of
reservation for SCs/STs in technical
institutions has been a failure and their
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

10
dropout rate is increasing; if so, the plan of
Government in this regard?
Agreement for child protection with
UNICEF
*28. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Government of India has entered into a new
agreement with UNICEF to check violence
against children and reduce the rate of HIV/
AIDS among adolescents during the next
five years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
set up child protection units in different
States under the Integrated Child Protection
Scheme;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether this programme would go a
long way to help SC/ST children, especially
the girls; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
High Court Bench at
Thiruvananthapuram
*29. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Kerala
Government has unanimously passed a
resolution and a joint memorandum of the
State Ministry and all parties in the State
demanding setting up of a High Court
Bench at Thiruvananthapuram, the capital
city of the State which was received by the
Government of India;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the reasons for not taking any steps
to set up a High Court Bench there?
Solar taxi
*30. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that one Mr.
Palmer is reported to have developed a
battery for solar taxi which, when charged,
can travel 400 kilometers at a speed of 90
kilometers per hour and is on a visit to
Poland en-route to various countries in
Europe and USA;
(b) if so, the detail on technology
gathered by the Indian scientists and
technocrats;
(c) whether it is also a fact that some
Indians have also invented solar energy
based petrol-less engine for vehicles and
submitted to Government for patent
registration; and
(d) if so, the action taken by
Government?
Arbitrary fees by private educational
institutions
†*31. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
fees are charged arbitrarily from the students
in the name of self-financed curricula by
private educational institutions;
(b) whether Government has received
any complaint in respect of the above;
(c) whether Government is
contemplating to implement in  private
colleges also the recommendations of the
committee, constituted by the UGC for
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

11
effecting equal fee structure in universities
and colleges of the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and by when
the same would be implemented?
Election to student unions
*32. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of Central Universities
where elections to student unions have been
conducted from January, 2007, till date,
university-wise;
(b) the details of Central Universities
where student unions are functioning at
present and where the same have been
dissolved, university-wise, from January,
2007 till date;
(c) the reasons for dissolution of the
unions, university-wise;
(d) when elections to the student unions
in the Jamia Millia Islamia, Banaras Hindu
University and Aligarh Muslim University
were conducted last;
(e) whether Government would conduct
elections in the Central Universities,
particularly in the above three universities
in this session;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor,
university-wise?
Foreign university centres
*33. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
foreign Universities intend to establish
centres in the country for graduate/post-
graduate courses and research activities;
(b) if so, whether there is any proposal
to make new regulations to allow these
universities to establish their centres in the
country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Suicides due to fear of examinations
*34. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether children are ending their life
for fear of exams and, if so, the number of
students who ended their life during 2006,
2007 and 2008, till date;
(b) whether Government has conducted
any study to ascertain the reasons behind
these deaths and taken any steps to
overcome such unfortunate deaths and, if
so, the number of complaints received and
the action taken thereon;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
change the present system of imparting
education and conducting examination/
evaluation to overcome the fear of
examination; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Importance of primary education
*35. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Supreme Court, in the
month of April, 2008, while dealing with
issue of 27 per cent OBC reservation in
higher education, did not lose sight of the
importance of primary education and felt
that a lot needs to be done to universalize
the fundamental right to education;
(b) if so, whether in the judgment,
stress has been given on primary and
secondary education so that proper

12
foundation for higher education can be
effectively laid;
(c) what other main points were made
in the judgment; and
(d) what steps Government proposes
to take in order to fulfil the constitutional
obligation of providing compulsory
education to the children of 6 to 14 years?
IGCC technology for power generation
*36. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether BHEL has entered into an
agreement with the Andhra Pradesh Power
Generation Corporation, to set up a 125
MW power, plants using the Integrated
Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC)
technology;
(b) if so, whether IGCC technology is
more thermal efficient than conventional
pulverized coal technology and is cost
effective too; and
(c) if so, the comparative figures
thereof?
Raising the retirement age of IIT
teachers
†*37. SHRI Y .P. TRIVEDI: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether IITs have raised the
retirement age of teachers by three years,
in order to maintain the required student-
teacher ratio;
(b) if so, the effective date thereof; and
(c) if not, the new measures being
adopted to meet the shortage of teachers?
Captive mines
*38. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether companies are given license
for mining of iron-ore in captive mines;
(b) if so, the details of the companies
which are given such licenses;
(c) whether proper assessment to
ascertain the quantum of iron-ore deposits
in these mines has been done;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, whether Government would
take comprehensive measures to assess the
quantum of deposits in such mines and, if
so, the details thereof?
Supply of equipment to power
generation companies
*39. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Prime
Minister has issued directions that State-
run companies, including Bharat Heavy
Electricals Ltd. should be given preference
in placement of bulk orders for power
equipment supply by all the power
generation companies in the country to
protect the interest of Domestic Power
Equipment Companies;
(b) if so, the details of mandatory
binding orders issued, so far, to all the power
generation companies;
(c) whether a monitoring cell would be
created in the Ministry to constantly
monitor placement orders with PSUs by
power generating companies;
(d) if so, the details of the proposed
monitoring cell; and
(e) if not, the reasons for not creating
such a monitoring cell?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

13
Status of tribal people in Andaman
and Nicobar Islands
*40. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the tribal
people in Andaman and Nicobar Islands
are extremely poor and are suffering for
want of food and clothing;
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 14th October, 2008 Secretary-General.
Asvina 22, 1930 (Saka)
(b) whether it is also a fact that young
tribal people, including women and children,
remain naked for want of clothing and beg
from passers-by in cars on A TR Road;
and
(c) if so, the measures proposed to
improve the plight particularly of girls and
women?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Food Processing Industries :—
Human Resource Development : 24, 27, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 37,
Law and Justice : 23, 29,
Mines : 21, 38,
Minority Affairs :—
New and Renewable Energy : 30,
Power : 25, 26, 36, 39,
Social Justice and Empowerment :—
Tribal Affairs : 40,
Women and Child Development : 22, 28.
MGIPMRND—3266RS—14.10.2008.
